units.title: Night cuts reach a fifth night as co-op points again to salt fog
units.author: courier
units.text: Households across the Sound lost power for the fifth night in six, with faults on the Gilliver spur, the Brackwater feeder and parts of north Port Ammet between eleven o'clock and three in the morning. Sound Power Co-op said all customers were back on supply by 03:20, and that crews had worked through the night on the coastal circuits.

units.author: courier
units.text: In a statement the co-op said the faults remained 'consistent with salt-fog corrosion on exposed coastal sections', made worse by the sudden cold. Engineers have been washing insulators on the Gilliver spur and replacing fittings 'where inspection identifies wear'. The co-op said the network was 'robust' and that the pattern of faults was being studied.

units.author: courier
units.text: Some customers question that explanation. 'We've had clear skies all week,' said one Lisle resident, who asked not to be named. 'If it's fog, where is it?' A retired surveyor who keeps a weather station near Carrow Point told the Courier his records show no fog on at least two of the nights when faults were logged, and humidity well below the level at which salt fog forms.

units.author: courier
units.text: Asked about this, the co-op said salt deposited during the fog earlier in the month could remain on equipment for days and cause tracking when temperatures fall sharply. It did not say how many faults had been recorded this month or whether further crews would be brought in from outside the region.

units.author: courier
units.text: Freezer and food losses can be claimed through the co-op's domestic losses scheme. Ammet District Council said schools would open as normal unless a head teacher decided otherwise, and asked residents to check on elderly neighbours during the cold snap, particularly those who rely on electric heating or powered medical equipment.

units.title: Night ferries to return with brighter decks
units.author: courier
units.text: Sound Lines will restart its night crossings between Port Ammet, Lisle and Gilliver tomorrow, almost a week after cutting the late sailings for what it called a crew welfare review. The 22:40 departure from Port Ammet will be the first to run.

units.author: courier
units.text: The company said the night vessel had been fitted with additional deck floodlights and a more powerful searchlight, and that temporary lighting towers had been installed at the Gilliver and Lisle slipways with the help of the harbour authority. The lighting is powered from the ship's main supply with a generator in reserve.

units.author: courier
units.text: Sound Lines did not publish the findings of the review. A spokesperson said the company had 'listened carefully to our crews' and that the changes reflected 'best practice for night operations on unlit infrastructure'. One crew member is understood to have left the company during the review period; Sound Lines said it did not discuss individual staff.

units.author: courier
units.text: Lisle commuters, more than three hundred of whom signed a petition for the late sailings to return, welcomed the news but said the week had been costly. 'I've paid for two water taxis and slept on my sister's sofa three times,' said one. 'I'd like the boat back and I'd like to be told why it went.'

units.title: Gilliver grows used to the lights on the Holm
units.author: soundfm
units.text: Residents of Gilliver say they have grown used to a new sight on the horizon: the lights of the clearance camp on Kittering Holm, nine kilometres offshore, which can be seen from the harbour through the night.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 'You look out last thing and there they are,' said one woman who lives on Harbour Row. 'A few white ones and one orange, low down, which I suppose is their fire. It's company, in a way. Nobody's lived out there in my lifetime, and now there's somebody awake over there when I am.'

units.author: soundfm
units.text: The island is being cleared of trees under a 30-day contract held by Grieve Land Services for its owner, Ardent Vale Holdings. Neither company responded to Sound FM's questions about how many people are working on the island or how long they will remain once the work is finished.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: Some in the village have taken to leaving a lamp lit in a front window, a custom Gilliver families say goes back generations and which has become more common during this month's night power cuts. 'It's manners,' one older resident told us. 'You let people know the house is awake.'

units.title: Dellow Court stairwell lights fixed, but tenants say unease remains
units.author: weypost
units.text: Lights in the stairwell of Dellow Court, the 14-storey tower block on the city's north estate, have stayed on for a week after an electrician replaced a faulty timer relay, the block's managers have confirmed.

units.author: weypost
units.text: Kerrow Estates said the relay on the riser serving floors six to eight had been 'identified as the cause of the intermittent lighting faults' and thanked residents 'for their patience during the investigation'. The company is checking timers in its other blocks across the city.

units.author: weypost
units.text: The residents' association welcomed the repair but said some tenants remained uneasy about using the stairs, even in daylight. 'A light fault is a maintenance issue,' said the association's secretary. 'People being nervous of their own stairwell is still an issue, and we'd like the landlord to take that seriously too.'

units.author: weypost
units.text: One family left the block earlier this month. Kerrow Estates said it did not comment on individual tenancies. The block's single lift, which has broken down repeatedly during the cold weather, was working at the time of writing.

units.title: Roundwood prices hold as big clearances stretch crews
units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Softwood roundwood prices at the Weyhaven port yards held steady this month despite several large clearance contracts coming to market at once, with buyers pointing to firm demand for pallet and fencing grades ahead of the spring building season.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Contractors say crews are stretched thin. 'Everybody's got a big job on and nobody's got spare saws,' said one regional site manager. Day rates for experienced fellers on remote contracts have risen to between $280 and $320, the journal understands, with accommodation on top.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Among the largest live contracts is Grieve Land Services' clearance of Kittering Holm, a six-kilometre island in the Marrow Sound, which the firm is carrying out on a 30-day schedule for a private owner. Grieve declined to give an update on progress, citing client confidentiality.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Island work adds cost at every stage. Logs must be landed by barge or stacked on site, and fuel, food and accommodation all depend on the weather. Brokers said they expected island timber to reach the yards later in the season, 'if it reaches them at all', since some private owners prefer to leave felled timber where it lies.

units.title: Gritters out for a fourth night as the cold holds
units.author: weypost
units.text: Weyhaven's gritting lorries were out for a fourth night as the calm, cold spell over the region continued, with temperatures falling to minus five on the city's outer estates and a hard frost on the river path.

units.author: weypost
units.text: The city council said main routes and bus corridors had been treated, but asked residents to take care on footpaths and estate roads, which are not on the priority list. Several tower blocks reported icy entrance ramps, and one bus depot said it had started its engines an hour early to keep them warm.

units.author: weypost
units.text: Forecasters expect the cold to hold for another day or two before milder, wetter air arrives from the west, bringing rain to most of the region and an end to the frosts, but also the risk of standing water on roads that are already cracked.

units.title: Live: power cuts across the Sound tonight
units.author: soundfm
units.text: 23:15. We're getting reports of power cuts in parts of Gilliver and along the Holm road. Sound Power Co-op's fault map shows about 400 customers affected. We'll update this page through the night as we hear more from listeners and from the co-op.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 00:05. The cut has spread to the Lisle pier area. Listeners on Lisle say the new lighting tower on the ferry slip has switched to its generator, which you can hear across the village. One describes it as 'like a lawnmower in the bedroom'.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 00:55. Sound Power says a crew is patrolling the Gilliver spur. No cause has been given yet. The overnight team here in the studio is running on backup power and we are staying on air, so keep your radios on if you've got batteries.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 01:50. Power is back for most of Gilliver. The fault map still shows about sixty properties off near the Holm road layby. Thank you to everyone who has messaged in. We can't read them all out, but we are reading them.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 03:15. The co-op says all customers are back on supply. That's the end of our live updates tonight. Look after each other, check on the neighbours in the morning, and see whether the freezer is still cold before you open it.

units.title: Market traders count the cost of the cold
units.author: courier
units.text: Traders at Tollinby's weekly market say the cold snap has cut footfall by about a third, with flower and vegetable stalls hit hardest as frost spoils stock set out on the tables before the eight o'clock opening.

units.author: courier
units.text: 'I lost two trays of primulas in one morning,' said one florist who has traded at the market for eleven years. 'People don't want to stand about in minus four. They grab their bread and their eggs and go home.' The cheese stall reported that business was, by contrast, 'never better'.

units.author: courier
units.text: The market committee has asked the council to let stallholders move into the covered corn exchange until the weather turns. The council said it would consider the request at next month's meeting, by which point the forecast suggests the frost will long have gone.

units.author: met
units.text: Forecast for the Marrow Sound, today and tonight. High pressure remains centred over the region. Dry, sunny and very cold, with light variable winds under 5 knots. Maximum 2 °C. Tonight clear with a widespread hard frost; minimum −5 °C inland, −2 °C on the coast. Isolated freezing fog possible in the Brackwater valley after 03:00; otherwise excellent visibility. Outlook: cold and calm, turning milder and wet later in the week.

units.author: met
units.text: Tides and small craft, Port Ammet reference. High water 04:12 (4.1 m) and 16:38 (4.3 m). Low water 10:27 and 22:51. Small-craft conditions good; sea state smooth. Ice reported on pontoons and slipway surfaces in the early morning. Take care when boarding and landing.

units.author: met
units.text: Evening update for the Marrow Sound. Clear and calm overnight with a hard frost; minimum −6 °C in sheltered inland valleys. No fog expected on the coast. Untreated roads and paths will be icy. Tomorrow: another bright, cold and still day, with cloud beginning to thicken from the west late in the evening.

units.author: ferry
units.text: Sound Lines service update. Night sailings on the Port Ammet - Lisle - Gilliver route resume tomorrow from the 22:40 Port Ammet departure. The night vessel has been fitted with additional deck lighting, and temporary lighting towers are in place at the Gilliver and Lisle slips. Daytime sailings run to the normal timetable today. Thank you for your patience.

units.author: ferry
units.text: Sound Lines: today's 15:10 Lisle - Gilliver sailing will depart about 10 minutes late due to icing on the Lisle linkspan. Crew are gritting the ramp. Foot passengers please use the handrail. All other sailings are running on time.

units.author: power
units.text: Sound Power Co-op: supply restored. Overnight interruptions affected customers in Gilliver, the Holm road area, Lisle pier and north Port Ammet between 23:08 and 03:14. All customers are now on supply. Faults are under investigation and are believed to be related to salt-fog corrosion on exposed coastal equipment. We apologise for the inconvenience.

units.author: power
units.text: Sound Power Co-op: insulator washing. Crews will be working on the Gilliver spur and the Holm road section today between 09:00 and 15:00. No planned interruption to supply. Please give crews room at the Holm road layby and do not park on the verge.

units.author: power
units.text: Sound Power Co-op: night advisory. Further interruptions are possible on coastal circuits tonight. If you lose supply, check our fault map before calling. Keep freezers closed. Never approach a fallen line. Customers on the priority services register will be contacted if an interruption lasts more than four hours.

units.author: power
units.text: Sound Power Co-op: unplanned interruption. Gilliver, Holm road and Lisle pier, from 23:12. Approximately 410 customers affected. A crew has been dispatched. Estimated restoration 01:30. We will update this notice.

units.author: power
units.text: Sound Power Co-op: update. Supply was restored to most customers in Gilliver and Lisle at 01:47. Around 60 customers near the Holm road layby remain off supply. A crew is on site and we expect full restoration within two hours.

units.author: council
units.text: Ammet District Council: waste collections. Recycling collections delayed earlier this week are being caught up. If your bin was not emptied on its scheduled day, please leave it at the kerbside and it will be collected by the end of the week. We thank residents for their patience.

units.author: council
units.text: Ammet District Council: gritting. Priority routes, including the Port Ammet - Tollinby road, the Brackwater junction and the Gilliver harbour road, will be treated from 18:00 tonight. The temporary signals at the Brackwater junction may fail during power interruptions; please treat the junction as unmarked and give way with care.

units.author: coast
units.text: Notice to mariners. Gilliver and Lisle slips: temporary lighting towers have been established at the head of each slip and will be exhibited from sunset to sunrise until further notice. Mariners approaching the slips at night are advised that the lighting may cause glare at close range. Approach at reduced speed.

units.author: coast
units.text: Notice to mariners. Skerry buoy, east of Gilliver in the channel towards Kittering Holm: the light is reported unlit. Mariners are advised to navigate with caution in the vicinity until the light is restored. A servicing visit is planned when conditions allow.

units.title: Timesheet received KH-01
units.author: grieve_payroll
units.text: Your timesheet for site KH-01, day 21, has been received and queued for processing. Crew day rate: $300 per worker per day. Piece rate: $100 per verified tree. Period 3 closes at the end of day 24. Statement detail is available on the payroll portal. This is an automated message. Please do not reply to this address.

units.title: Outstanding crew wages: reminder
units.author: grieve_payroll
units.text: Payment reminder. Ref GLS-AR-22. Site: KH-01. Our records show crew wages outstanding on the site account. Under the contract schedule, crew day rates are payable daily. Outstanding wages at the close of period 3 will be referred to Operations. This is an automated message. Please do not reply to this address.

units.title: Your payment date is changing
units.author: lyle_insurance
units.text: Dear Policyholder, following our annual review of collection dates, your next premium for policy LY-4471-0938 will be collected two days later than usual. You don't need to do anything. Peace of mind, on schedule! Small print: this notice does not alter your cover. Please read your policy wording for full terms and exclusions.

units.title: Frost week! Five ways to keep your camp cosy
units.author: camp_supply_news
units.text: Frost week is here! Our five favourite ways to keep your camp cosy: 1. Insulate under you, not just over you! 2. Keep a flask by the bed. 3. Bank your stove before you sleep. 4. Hang a thermal curtain across the door. 5. Never let the lights go out! Our Beacon range runs right through the longest nights. Stay warm out there!

units.title: Ammet District Council: your weekly news
units.author: council_news
units.text: This week: Bins: catch-up collections are under way; leave missed bins out. Roads: gritting continues on priority routes; the Brackwater junction signals remain temporary. Sound Power works: some areas may see short interruptions overnight while the co-op carries out works on the coastal network. Consultation: have your say on the Port Ammet seafront plan. Photo competition: this month's theme is 'Winter Light'. Entries close soon!

units.title: Reminder: winter warmth grants
units.author: council_news
units.text: A reminder that the council's winter warmth grants close at the end of the month. Households with a member over 75, or with young children, may be eligible for help towards heating costs or an emergency heater. Applications take ten minutes online. Know someone who might qualify? Please pass this on.

units.title: Next supply run
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, a few things for the next supply run: - The skipper says the Gilliver slip was icy this morning, so allow extra time for unloading and keep the crew off the boat ramp until he's tied up. - The anti-gel additive from last week's manifest is on board again in case you're short. - If there's anything you need that isn't on the list, tell me by noon tomorrow. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Head office circular: cold-weather working
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, head office has asked me to send this to every site lead, so please don't read anything into it: - Breaks indoors, hot drinks, and check each other for cold hands and feet. - No one works alone after dark. - Keep a working torch on every person. - Log any injury, however small. I've ticked the box saying you've received it. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Generator hours
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, accounts have asked for the generator hours on KH-01 for the period, so they can reconcile the fuel invoices. If you can read the hour meter and pop the number in the site log tonight, that's all they need. No problem if it's higher than usual; I know the nights are long. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Numbers before the client call
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, just checking where we are on numbers ahead of the client call tomorrow. If the tally on the system is up to date by tonight, that would be a big help. I know the cold isn't making anything easier. Just over a week left on the schedule, so every day counts from here. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Past halfway
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, quick one: the tally shows the Holm is past the halfway mark. That's a good place to be with just over a week to go, and I've told head office so. Keep the pace steady, keep everyone warm, and don't let anyone take risks to make the last stretch faster. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: The tally
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, I'll be straightforward: head office is worried. The tally shows less than a quarter of the island cleared with just over a week to go, which is a long way off the schedule. Can you tell me what you need? More saws, better kit, anything I can put on the next boat. Please reply in the site log tonight. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Crew numbers
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, I've been asked again by head office whether we can replace the crew member who left. I've tried three agencies. Nobody with a ticket will take an island job this late in the contract, and I won't send someone untrained. Please plan the remaining work around the crew you have, and look after them. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Sound FM piece
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, Sound FM ran a short piece today about people in Gilliver watching the camp lights. It's harmless and nobody here is bothered by it. A reminder only: if anyone calls, emails, or turns up on the slip with questions, please point them to me or to head office, however friendly they are. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: mum's home!!
units.author: sam
units.text: hiya, Mum's home. The new hip is 'very stiff and very expensive', according to her. She's on the sofa with the frame next to her like a little fence and the dog has decided to sleep across her feet, which the physio said not to allow, so we're losing that battle already. I made shepherd's pie and she said it was nearly as good as hers, which is the nicest thing she's said to me in a decade. love, S x

units.author: sam
units.text: me again. Sound FM had a thing on about people in Gilliver watching your camp lights at night and putting lamps in their windows. I don't know if that's sweet or a bit odd. I've put one in mine too, which is silly, because Tollinby is miles away and you can't possibly see it. It's the big lamp from the hall. anyway. ignore me. love, S x

units.author: sam
units.text: the power went off here just after eleven and Mum said 'oh good, an adventure' and then fell asleep. The dog and I sat in the dark and listened to the fridge stop. it came back at half one. I hope you've got proper lights out there and a proper heater. are you sleeping? love, S x

units.title: important dog update
units.author: sam
units.text: important dog update: the cheese tactic has been discovered and banned by Mum, who caught him at it from the sofa. He has responded by sitting next to Mum instead and sighing at her, which is working better, because she's a soft touch on painkillers. I'm sending you a photo in my head. It's a very good photo. S x

units.title: Sorry if this is strange
units.author: morrow_unknown
units.text: Hello. Sorry if this is strange. I might be wrong about all of it. I live in Gilliver and I read the forums at night, and I think you might be the person in charge on the Holm. Grieve's addresses all follow the same pattern, and a site lead's email was on an old tender notice, so I guessed. I don't want anything. I only wanted to say that someone over here is awake too. Morrow

units.author: morrow_unknown
units.text: I should have said in the first one: I'm not a reporter and I'm not anyone from the company. I do data entry on nights, from home. I'm not going to tell anyone I wrote to you. I won't write every night. Sorry again. Morrow

units.title: From the archive: a correction, 1953
units.author: courier_archivist
units.text: Editor's note: in the spring of 1953 the paper reported that the Lights Board survey party 'will camp on the Holm for a fortnight'. The following week it printed the short correction below, on page two, under the weather. It is reproduced in full because readers have asked whether the paper ever explained the survey party's arrangements. It did not; it only corrected them. G. Faulds.

units.author: courier_archivist
units.text: Correction. In our report of last week concerning the Lights Board survey of Kittering Holm, we stated that the survey party would camp upon the island. We are asked to make clear that the party is returning to Gilliver each evening by arrangement with a local boatman, and that no camp has been established. We regret the error.

units.title: Penhallow wage book: loose leaves, December 1894
units.author: camp_clerk_1894
units.text: Wages, week ending Decr 15th. Trewin 6 days, 15s. Doble 6 days, 15s. Pascoe 5 days, 12s 6d, one day lost to his hand. Rowe brothers, paid off the 11th at their own asking, 2 days each, 5s each, paid in coin at the landing. Cook, 7 days, 14s. Mr Coad signs. Received with thanks, Doble his mark.

units.author: camp_clerk_1894
units.text: Wages, week ending Decr 22nd. 14 men and the cook, all paid full, no deductions save for Pascoe's tobacco. Christmas allowance of one shilling each from the company, and a goose, which the cook spoilt. Oil bought: 4 gallons, being more than the usual, the lamps burning all night in the long hut now by Mr Coad's order.

units.title: Carrow Point log, December 1906 (excerpts, cont.)
units.author: carrow_keeper
units.text: 5th. 00:00 calm, vis 14 miles, barometer 30.48. Lamp burning well. Hard frost. 01:40 Gilliver lights all out save the one window at the harbour end. Remarks: Two on the shore road at 02:20, below the light, standing. Did not hail them. Assistant came up at the change of watch and stood with me at the glass. Neither of us remarked on it.

units.title: Miss Arnell's notebook: Kittering Holm survey (cont.)
units.author: naturalist_1923
units.text: Eighth day. Rain overnight, cleared by nine. Set a line of twelve marked sticks in the browse at the north landing to see if anything would nibble them. [sketch: stick with notch] By four o'clock: nothing. Rabbits absent too, which I had not noted before and ought to have. Pengelly asked to leave at half past three. I said four. We compromised, as usual, on his time.

units.title: Amos Rendle's diary, 1936 (excerpts, cont.)
units.author: fisher_diary_1930s
units.text: Feb 4. Still calm. Prices down, 2s the box. Will came out on the day tide and was cheerful as anything, so it is only the nights. Mother says leave him be, her brother were the same one winter and grew out of it. Mended the long net in the loft by the lamp. Mother kept the window lamp in all night as usual.

units.title: LB-0412 and LB-0415: Gilliver harbour hydrophone recordings
units.author: lowband_archivist
units.text: LB-0412. Date: March 2004. Location: Gilliver harbour, east pontoon. Kit: home-made hydrophone, minidisc. Duration: 22:40. Content: prop wash from two creel boats, hull slap, a steady tonal hum near 50 Hz throughout. Recordist's note: 'Fish market chiller, confirmed with the market manager.' Curator's note: a useful reference for anyone recording at the same spot.

units.author: lowband_archivist
units.text: LB-0415. Date: August 2004. Location: as LB-0412. Duration: 18:05. Content: as above, but the 50 Hz hum is absent for the whole recording. Recordist's note: 'Market shut for refit that week.' Curator's note: so the earlier attribution seems sound, at least for 2004. Equipment on the quay has changed several times since.

units.title: Gilliver Oral History Project (1976): tape 23, side A
units.author: oral_history_1970s
units.text: Interviewer: Did the young ones get up to mischief on the harbour? / Mr W. Rowe (b. 1909): Oh, always. We used to dare each other to stand on the end of the slip after dark with your back to the water. Count to a hundred. / Interviewer: Did you do it? / Mr R.: Course I did. Got to forty. [laughs] My brother got to a hundred, he said. Nobody was counting for him.

units.author: oral_history_1970s
units.text: Interviewer: Why only to forty? / Mr R.: Cold. [pause] Well. You'd hear the water behind you and you'd think it was someone come up the slip. It never was. That was the point of the dare. / Interviewer: Do children still do it? / Mr R.: I hope not. My mother leathered me for it. She said you don't stand where they stand. I never knew what she meant.

units.title: Talk: Holm timber camp, wage book leaves
units.author: hist_wiki_pell
units.text: Talk note. The newly transcribed wage book leaves for December show sums 'held' for men who left before the end of a week. Held wages were a standing grievance in timber camps of the period and a common cause of walkouts. I suggest the article note this alongside the lamp anecdotes, which have had rather more than their share of attention. Pell.

units.title: Talbot survey (1953): appendix A, party diary
units.author: relay_engineer_1950s
units.text: Day 1. Landed 08:10 at the north landing with chainman, two labourers and theodolite. Cut sight line to the knoll by 11:30. Bearings taken. Boat returned 15:45 at the party's request, an hour earlier than arranged, the light being poor. Day 2. Levelling along the ridge path. Cold, still. Boat at 15:30. Labourer Coombe asked for a second torch to be carried.

units.author: relay_engineer_1950s
units.text: Day 3. Proposed tower position pegged at H/7. Trial pit dug to 1.1 m: peat over shale, suitable. At the party's request the plan to sleep in the old curing house was abandoned and the boat engaged for each evening. The additional boat hire is entered under contingencies. Day 4. Fog until 10:00. No work possible before then.
